svg.title: E4 / A thick continuous facing buffer
svg.desc: Concept investigation only, not to scale or evaluated CAD. Normal black TPU, no thickness cap. Blue is facing material, green is compliant structure, brown is solid corner or perimeter material. Process and assembly views show proposals, not verified toolpaths.

g.text: E4 / A thick continuous facing buffer
A one-piece comparison using the newly unconstrained thickness.
SVG PROPOSAL • 21 Oct 2026 • black TPU • thickness free • no new model or slice
One piece: give the face its own generous continuous material region
Backing + hollow core
Thick face
Contents
Move core junctions farther from the face.
Room for several ordinary-width paths.
Keep an air/compliant core — not solid C.
Fill the corner lands and taper their ends.
Dashed lines show space for lanes,
not guaranteed slicer paths.
The printable part count stays low; the coupling remains
One cup + one matching pad.
A broad material buffer replaces the very thin face.
Core features are still bonded to that same material.
This is a conservative control, not full separation.
What this buys — and what it does not establish
Example budget: 1.6 facing + 2.0 compliant core + 0.8 backing ≈ 4.4 mm.
Partial change: surface is farther from core junctions; direct material bonds remain.
Trade-off: more material/stiffness, possibly only a smaller visible pattern.
Weakest departure of these four; useful as a control, not the main creative answer.
Solid corners + gradual transition required. Dimensions are discussion examples; Classic qualification comes later.
